newsitem.title: CANADA: Plant outages continue to boost Canada spot gas.
newsitem.headline: Plant outages continue to boost Canada spot gas.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices in the west rose again on Wednesday as a big plant outage in British Columbia and several smaller ones in Alberta tightened supplies, traders said.
Westcoast Energy's 750 million cubic feet a day Fort Nelson gas plant in northeastern B.C. was not expected to wrap up a maintenace run until June 18.

The outage turned a normal 100 MMCFD flow of gas into Alberta from B.C. into a 25 MMCFD flow out of Alberta, a Calgary-based trader said, adding several Alberta plants in the 20-50 MMCFD range were also in turnarounds.
He said Wednesday's stronger price was also due to the outage of a 200 MMCFD Amoco Canada-operated plant at Windfall, Alberta.
"The field receipts just aren't showing up right now," he said.
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was quoted at C$1.55/1.56 per gigajoule, up from C$1.52/1.54 on Tuesday and about on par with last week.
July AECO was also talked about 1 cent higher than Tuesday at C$1.51. The summer term was discussed slightly higher at C$1.515/1.52.

The Fort Nelson outage continued to spark prices for gas exported at the Sumas, Wash. border point as well. Sumas spot gas was quoted at US$1.34/1.38 per million British thermal units, up about 6 cents from Tuesday.
Deals at B.C.'s compressor station 2 were done anywhere between C$1.60 and C$1.70 per GJ, said a marketer with a Calgary-based producer.

In eastern Canada, prices across the TransCanada PipeLines Ltd eastern zone were talked in the low US$2.30s per mmBtu in light trade. That was up about 2 cents from Tuesday. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
